title: fix(deps): stop layout and plugin-dashboard installing a React of their own
body:
Fixes #8303

`@object-ui/layout` and `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` were each making two contradictory statements in one manifest: asking the host for React as a **peer** (`^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`) and **also** pinning an exact React 19 of their own in `dependencies`. The peer range is what a consumer reads; the pin is what their installer acts on. A consumer on React 18 therefore satisfied the peer range and **still** got a second, pinned React 19 pulled into their graph on these two packages' account.

Two React copies in one tree is the classic cause of `Invalid hook call` — and the failure is not at install time. It is at first render, in the consumer's own component, with nothing pointing back at these manifests.

`react` moves to `devDependencies` at the same pin (`19.2.8`). **`peerDependencies` is untouched, byte for byte.**

## The population reading, re-derived rather than inherited

Re-measured on `origin/main` at `348725a7c` across all four `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs (46 packages), not carried over from the card's `e2409120f` reading:

| shape | count | packages |
|:--|--:|:--|
| declares a `react` peer **and** pins `react` in `dependencies` | **2** | `layout`, `plugin-dashboard` |
| declares a `react-dom` peer **and** pins it in `dependencies` | **0** | objectui#8198 already took that half |
| pins `react` in `dependencies` with **no** react peer | 5 | `runner`, `site`, 3 `examples/*` |

That last row is the control that keeps this narrow, and it is a refinement of the card: the card says "no other released package does this", and that is true **of the contradiction**. Three packages plus the apps do pin React in `dependencies` — they simply declare no peer beside it. They are applications that *supply* React rather than libraries that *ask* for it: one statement, not two, and correctly untouched here.

Against the 20+ sibling libraries this converges on the existing house shape. `app-shell`, `auth`, `collaboration`, `i18n`, `mobile` and `permissions` already carry `react` in `devDependencies` at exactly this pin.

## The pin, and proof it can fail

`scripts/__tests__/react-peer-range-norm-3741.test.ts` gains the invariant. That file was already the same-class guard — it owns React manifest norms across the fixed version group, already walks the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs, and already governs `react` + `react-dom` — so this is a second assertion on an existing guard, **not a new gate**.

It asserts the **contradiction**, not "React in `dependencies`". Widening it further would go red on the five applications above for doing the right thing.

Ablation, both legs, with the mutation proven on disk before the run and the restore proven by state:

```
HEAD blobs: layout=b7607ba8c… plugin-dashboard=fab7a1a00…
BEFORE mutation:  layout deps.react = (absent)      dashboard deps.react = (absent)
[mutate: git checkout 348725a7c -- both manifests]
AFTER mutation:   git diff HEAD: 2 files changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
                  layout deps.react = 19.2.8        dashboard deps.react = 19.2.8
ABLATION_VITEST_EXIT=1
[restore: git checkout HEAD -- both manifests]  git diff HEAD --stat: (empty)
```

Pre-fix — `Tests 2 failed | 3 passed (5)`, both new assertions red, naming both packages:

```
AssertionError: A package may ask its host for React as a peer, or install a React of its own, but not both:

@object-ui/layout (packages/layout/package.json) declares "react" as a peer (^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0) AND pins it in dependencies ("19.2.8")
@object-ui/plugin-dashboard (packages/plugin-dashboard/package.json) declares "react" as a peer (^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0) AND pins it in dependencies ("19.2.8")
```

The three pre-existing assertions stayed **green** through the mutation, which is what says the two new ones are the discriminating part rather than the file being broken. Post-fix: `Tests 5 passed (5)`.

## Two greens that are not readings of this

Both instruments below are green on this shape **by construction**, and neither green was evidence the defect was absent:

- **`check:unused-deps`** asks whether a declared runtime dependency has a *consumer*. `react` is imported by both packages, so the declaration has one. This is exactly why objectui#8198 could see and remove the `react-dom` half from these same two manifests and could not see this one — that card's licence covered declarations with **no** consumer.
- **`check-changeset-presence.mjs`** reads an eight-field allowlist (`sideEffects`, `exports`, `main`, `module`, `types`, `files`, `peerDependencies`, `engines`) that deliberately excludes `dependencies`. Its verdict on this very branch: `0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved … no changeset is owed.` Its own docblock states the trade rather than claiming invisibility — *"a runtime dependency bump can be just as user-visible as any of the eight, and this gate still does not see it."*

The changeset here is therefore **owed by the house rule, not demanded by the gate**. It is `patch` on both packages, following `.changeset/5753-providers-drop-spec-dep.md`, which removed a `dependencies` edge from a published package at the same level. Per AGENTS.md's version-alignment rule no changeset in this repo declares `major`; `changeset:check` confirms.

## Verification

| check | exit | verdict line |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/react-peer-range-norm-3741.test.ts` | 0 | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 5 passed (5)` |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/layout --filter=@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` | 0 | `Tasks: 15 successful, 15 total` (includes the `^build` closure) |
| `vitest run packages/layout/ packages/plugin-dashboard/` | 0 | `Test Files 122 passed (122)` · `Tests 1119 passed (1119)` |
| `check:phantom-deps` | 0 | `Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.` |
| `check:unused-deps` | 0 | `Every gated declaration has a consumer in the package that declares it.` |
| `check:lockfile-integrity` | 0 | `VERDICT clean — no @objectstack/* identity moved backward and no package gained a copy.` |
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 | `no changeset is owed` (quoted above — the gate is blind here on purpose) |
| `changeset:check` | 0 | `All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` · `No changeset declares a major bump.` |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 | `OK (scanned 7088 tracked text file(s))` |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 | `NOT GOVERNED — 5 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |

Every heavy run went through the container's shared verify lock; exit codes were captured before any pipe. `@object-ui/layout` has **no** `test` script but 21 test files, so its suite was run from the repo root — `pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout test` matches zero scripts and exits 0 having run nothing.

`pnpm install` moved `react` between the two importers' sections in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and nothing else (6 insertions, 6 deletions). The `react-dom` line that remains under each importer's lockfile `dependencies` is pnpm's `auto-install-peers=true` bookkeeping for a resolved peer, not a manifest entry — confirmed against `plugin-charts`, which declares both React peers with no manifest edge and shows the identical lockfile shape.

## Position axis

Verdict **(B) — nothing stale.** Judged by anchor, not by line number, on both carrier classes:

- `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` `UNGATED_EXAMPLES` — the confirmed stored carrier the census cannot see. Its 90 keys include three under `packages/layout`, all pointing at `.tsx` sources (`AppSchemaRenderer`, `NavigationRenderer`, `ResponsiveGrid`). This diff touches no `.tsx` file, so none of those lines move.
- `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` — run on the branch **and** on a real `git merge --no-ff` result tree against `main`; the two drift sets are byte-identical (`diff` exit 0). All reported drift is pre-existing and names none of the touched files.
- A direct repo-wide grep for line-numbered citations naming any touched file returns **no matches** (grep exit 1, captured before the pipe), on the branch and on the merge tree alike.

## Clause-② — `yes`

Judged from this diff rather than inherited, and it does **not** rest on the mechanical floor (no new exported symbol, and this *removes* an entry rather than adding a key):

1. `package.json` ships inside the tarball, and `dependencies` is the field a consumer's installer acts on. This change alters **what every consumer of two published packages installs** — that is a published-contract change in substance, whatever the changeset gate's allowlist happens to cover.
2. The gate's exclusion of `dependencies` is a documented, accepted trade — quoted above — not a finding that the field is invisible. Reading its green as "no contract moved" would be the same instrument-blindness error this card exists to correct.
3. There is a real delivered-behaviour change on the consumer side, in both directions: a React 18 consumer stops getting a second React, and anyone who was implicitly relying on these packages to supply React at all now gets only the peer demand.

`needs:contract-review` is attached to both carriers — this PR and objectui#8303 — in the same act.

## ⚠️ Measured cost of this change — two red checks, ONE root cause — **now closed in this PR**

⭐ Kept verbatim below as the record of how the coupling was found and what was measured about the alternatives. The ruling on objectui#8919 landed as **option A**, and the gate change that implements it is the section after this one. Both checks are green on `8428db85f`.

Rebased onto the moved base first: `origin/main` advanced to `4fa0eb9c4` while this was open, so `main` was merged in (`edf2aced3`) and **every reading below was retaken with both trees at that same base**. An A/B across two different trees would not have been comparable.

### The complete red list, enumerated rather than relayed

Taken from `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/commits/…/check-runs?per_page=100` on the head, because a per-check CI notification is a subset by construction:

```
34 checks total  —  29 success · 3 skipped · 2 failure
failure: Doc Snippet Type Check
failure: Test (shard 1/4)
```

Two, and only two. Both are the **same defect in this PR**, so this is one problem, not two.

### Both reds are one cause

`Test (shard 1/4)` is not a separate breakage. It is `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts:1255` — the **doc-snippet gate's own pin test** — asserting the identical invariant and receiving the identical 34 entries:

```
the ROOT BOUND … > no COVERED snippet imports a specifier that only the root declares
AssertionError: expected [ …(34) ] to deeply equal []
+   "content/docs/core/schema-renderer.mdx:98 react",
+   … 32 more …
+   "README.md:223 react",
```

100 of that file's 101 tests still pass. So the gate script's exit code and this unit test are two carriers of one invariant, and one fix moves both.

### A/B on matched trees, the gate's own summary lines verbatim

```
main   4fa0eb9c4   Root bound:     no block imports a specifier that resolves only through this repository's ROOT manifest.
                   Semantic phase: 638 of 638 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
                   -> Doc Snippet Type Check exit 0 · check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts exit 0 (101 passed)

branch edf2aced3   Root bound:     34 block(s) import a specifier that resolves only through the ROOT manifest (react)
                                   and were NOT semantically checked.
                   Semantic phase: 604 of 638 block(s) judged, 1 failed.
                   -> Doc Snippet Type Check exit 1 · check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts exit 1 (1 failed | 100 passed)
```

The mechanism is a one-specifier delta the gate prints itself: `Third-party resolution: 89 specifier(s) mapped …` on main against `88 …` here, from the same 34 imported packages, with all of the gate's own controls reading identically on both sides. The single specifier that left the map is `react`.

**`packages/layout` and `packages/plugin-dashboard` were the only two published packages declaring `react` in `dependencies`, so between them they were supplying `react` type-resolution for the entire documentation corpus.** The gate builds one program-wide specifier map from `dependencies` only — deliberately, "not `peerDependencies`, not `devDependencies`". Removing the contradiction removes the map entry. Only 2 of the 34 refused blocks are in the READMEs of the two packages this card touches; the other 32 sit in 19 files belonging to packages it does not.

The 34 span 21 files: `packages/providers/README.md` (4), `packages/auth/README.md` (4), `content/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md` (3), `packages/react/README.md` (2), `packages/react-runtime/README.md` (2), `packages/i18n/README.md` (2), `packages/app-shell/README.md` (2), root `README.md` (2), and one each in `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md`, `packages/plugin-chatbot/README.md`, `packages/layout/README.md`, `packages/fields/README.md`, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx`, `content/docs/guide/user-state-persistence.md`, `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`, `content/docs/guide/schema-playground.md`, `content/docs/guide/plugin-development.md`, `content/docs/guide/component-registry.md`, `content/docs/fields/location.mdx`, `content/docs/core/theme-schema.mdx`, `content/docs/core/schema-renderer.mdx`. The one semantic failure is `packages/react-runtime/README.md:72:36`, `TS2307: Cannot find module 'react'` — a block that already uses the stand-in pattern and reaches the semantic phase only because the bound scanner does not treat `typeof import()` as an import.

### The gate's recommended remedy was tested, and it does not work for `react`

The refusal names stand-ins, and names `packages/layout/README.md` "Usage with React Router" as the worked example. That example is now itself one of the 34 refused blocks — it imports `ComponentType` and `ReactNode` from `react` precisely *because* the package declared `react` in `dependencies`.

Applying the remedy to it as a throwaway trap-guarded probe (restored; `git diff HEAD` empty, blob back to `cd39170bb`) moved the block out of the bound — `Root bound: 33`, `Semantic phase: 605 of 638` — and straight into **6 new semantic errors**:

```
packages/layout/README.md:224:6  TS2786: 'BrowserRouter' cannot be used as a JSX component.
  Its type 'ComponentType<{ children?: unknown; }>' is not a valid JSX element type.
    Type 'ComponentType<...>' is not assignable to type '(props: any) => ReactNode | Promise[ReactNode]'.
      Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'ReactNode | Promise[ReactNode]'.
```

(The two `Promise` generics are spelled with square brackets in that quote only — GitHub body sanitising eats angle-bracket fragments, so the original would not survive the round trip. Nothing else in the message is changed.)

That is structural. A stand-in used **as a JSX component** must be typed so its return is assignable to React's real `ReactNode`, and React's real types are exactly what left the map. JSX itself keeps compiling — which is why 604 blocks still pass — because the JSX runtime types arrive through the root, not through this map; so such a block can neither import React's types nor hand-roll them. Classifying all 34: **27 contain JSX** and are in the class just measured as failing; only **7** have no JSX, and several of those import hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `forwardRef`) whose real generic signatures a stand-in would also have to reproduce to check anything. `@types/react` is in **zero** packages' `dependencies` repo-wide, so React's type vocabulary is unreachable by the map by any route.

The repository had already registered the shape of this: the pin test's own header (objectui#8059) says the refusal "came to name two remedies, one of which **reads as impossible on a peer** (the package DOES declare it, in a field this map does not read)". This measures that "reads as impossible" as *is* impossible, for 27 of 34.

### There is no declared-debt route either

`check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts:1255` asserts `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` flat — **no exemption list, no ledger, no reason field**. So the 34 cannot be recorded as accepted debt even if someone wanted to; the invariant is absolute and a test holds it.

### ⛔ What was deliberately NOT done

No green was manufactured. Not declared `fragment` (the gate's stated last resort — it stops the whole block compiling, the documented package's own surface included, which is a larger coverage loss than the one it hides, and it would silence the pin test by removing the blocks from the compiled set). Not skipped, disabled or exempted. Not reverted to `dependencies`, which reinstates the defect. `peerDependencies` untouched throughout. And not routed through a root declaration: the 2026-08-24 ruling on objectui#6120 rejects declaring a specifier at the repository root to make a checker pass, by name.

**This was a trade-off between the correctness of two published packages' dependency declarations and the type coverage of 34 documentation blocks, and it was a ruling rather than an implementation choice — so it was referred, on objectui#8919, rather than decided here. It has since been ruled: option A. The implementation is the next section.** The gate's own header anticipates one possible answer's shape: `dependencies`-only "fails CLOSED, and widening it later is a visible edit with a reason, not a silent drift." Whether `react` — a peer a consumer of a React component library must by definition already have — is that reason is the open question, and it is not this card's to answer.

## ⭐ The ruling, implemented — the specifier map now reads REQUIRED peers (objectui#8919, option A)

Commit `8428db85f`, on top of a real `git merge --no-ff origin/main` (`4b59f15d3`, `bbe285ee7` merged in, no conflicts). Every reading below was retaken on that merge result, not on the pre-merge base.

### The resolver change

`deriveDeclaredDependencyPaths` built the third-party map from `dependencies` only. It now also maps a specifier an imported package **REQUIRES of its consumer**, and only that class — all three conditions, or it is not mapped:

1. the specifier is named in that package's own `peerDependencies`;
2. its `peerDependenciesMeta` does **not** mark it `optional`;
3. it resolves — from inside that package's own directory, the same probe `dependencies` uses — to a declaration file outside any package's `src/`.

`requiredPeerSpecifiers()` is the new named predicate for (1)+(2). The peer half runs as a **SECOND pass** over the imported packages, after every `dependencies` entry of every owner is already decided, so it can only ever **add** a specifier: it cannot re-own an existing mapping or re-resolve one from a different directory. A new pin holds that ordering over a tree where a peer of the alphabetically-first package and a dependency of the second name the same specifier — `dependencies` wins.

### The reason written into the source, as the header asked for

That edge reserved the widening in these words: dependencies-only "fails CLOSED, and **widening it later is a visible edit with a reason, not a silent drift**". The reason now lives in the file, under three headings a new pin requires to be present — `THE CLASS IT NOW RESOLVES`, `WHY THAT IS SOUND`, `WHAT STAYS CLOSED`:

- **Why it is sound.** The map's one question is whether a reader of the documented package can resolve the specifier, and a REQUIRED peer answers it yes. It is not an optional extra the reader may lack: the package declares it cannot function without it, npm 7+ and pnpm (`auto-install-peers=true` here) install it, and a reader who has not supplied one is holding an install the package itself calls broken. It therefore reaches every reader who can use the package **at all** — the same reachability a `dependencies` entry has, arriving through the reader's own tree instead of the package's. On a React component library the case makes itself: a consumer with no `react` cannot render one node of any package documented here.
- **What stays closed, so this is a class and not a licence.** An **optional** peer is exactly what the old reason described — a requirement the consumer may legitimately not meet — and stays unmapped. A `devDependency` reaches no consumer and stays unmapped. A required peer that resolves to no declaration file stays unresolvable rather than approximated. Every specifier no imported package names in either field is still refused by the bound. **Nothing was declared at the repository root**; the 2026-08-24 ruling on objectui#6120 rejects that route by name and it stays rejected.
- **The widening is readable off a green.** Both gates that share this resolver now print how many mapped specifiers came from the peer half, every run. A pin asserts that sentence exists.

### Both failing checks, on matched trees

| instrument | before (`4b59f15d3`) | after (`8428db85f`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` | **exit 1** · `Root bound: 34 block(s) … (react) and were NOT semantically checked` · `Semantic phase: 604 of 638 block(s) judged, 1 failed` | **exit 0** · `Root bound: no block imports a specifier that resolves only through this repository's ROOT manifest.` · `Semantic phase: 638 of 638 block(s) judged, 0 failed` |
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts` | **exit 1** · `Tests 1 failed \| 100 passed (101)` · `expected [ …(34) ] to deeply equal []` | **exit 0** · `Tests 107 passed (107)` |

`Third-party resolution: 88 specifier(s) …` becomes `93 specifier(s) …, 5 of them from a REQUIRED peerDependency this workspace resolves`. The five, measured rather than assumed: `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`, `react-grid-layout`, `tailwindcss`. The one semantic failure that was left (`packages/react-runtime/README.md:72`, `TS2307: Cannot find module 'react'`) is gone with them, so the corpus is back to the coverage `main` had — 638 of 638 — with the manifest defect fixed rather than reinstated.

The derived build filter is **byte-identical** before and after in both gates (`diff` exit 0): the widening grows what resolves, not what CI builds.

### ⭐ The bright line: the gate can still report failures

A resolver that resolves everything would be worthless, so this is measured, not asserted. Four blocks were injected into one covered document (`content/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md`), trap-guarded, with the mutation proven on disk before the run (marker count 0 -> 4; blob `fe98cec31` -> `9f4b2ab6a`) and the restore proven by state afterwards (`git diff HEAD` empty, blob back to `fe98cec31`, marker count 0):

```
GATE_WITH_INJECTION_EXIT=1
Root bound:     1 block(s) import a specifier that resolves only through the ROOT manifest (vitest)
Semantic phase: 641 of 642 block(s) judged, 3 failed

[bound]     troubleshooting.md:389  imports 'vitest' … resolve only through this repository's ROOT package.json
[semantic]  troubleshooting.md:397:33  TS2307: Cannot find module '@floating-ui/react-dom' …
[semantic]  troubleshooting.md:405:14  TS2322: Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'.
[semantic]  troubleshooting.md:411:50  TS2322: Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'.
```

Each injection answers a different way this could have gone wrong:

- **A** — a specifier only the repository ROOT declares (`vitest`) is still **refused by the bound**, and still kept out of the semantic program.
- **B** — a specifier installed here but declared by no imported package (`@floating-ui/react-dom`) still fails **TS2307**. Resolution did not widen into `node_modules`.
- **C** — the decisive one for this change. A block importing the **newly mapped** `react` and misusing it goes red with a real **TS2322**. The mapping supplies React's real types; it did not resolve `react` to `any`, which is the failure mode that would have made every one of the 34 blocks green without checking anything.
- **D** — an ill-typed block against a workspace package still fails, so the pre-existing capability is intact.

The gate's own five controls are unmoved and still red where they must be: `sentinel` TS2305, `undeclared` (`@floating-ui/react-dom`) TS2307, `root-declared` (`vitest`) TS2307, `resolution` landing on `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts`, `positive` clean. Neither control specifier is a peer of anything — a new pin asserts that for **both**, in **both** fields the map now reads, with `react` as its known positive so the two zeros are readings rather than an empty probe.

### Ablation — the peer half is what does the work

One-line mutation of `requiredPeerSpecifiers` to return `[]`, trap-guarded, mutation proven on disk (blob `69a2c372d` -> `089f67b3e`, marker count 1) and restore proven by state (`git diff HEAD` empty, blob back to `69a2c372d`, marker count 0):

```
GATE_ABLATED_EXIT=1
Third-party resolution: 88 specifier(s) …, 0 of them from a REQUIRED peerDependency …
Root bound:     34 block(s) … (react) and were NOT semantically checked.
Semantic phase: 604 of 638 block(s) judged, 1 failed.
PIN_ABLATED_EXIT=1  — 5 failed (the four new peer pins, plus the root-bound pin)
```

Exactly the pre-change reading returns, so the 34 are closed by this predicate and not by anything else in the diff.

### The shared resolver, and what else was run

`scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` **imports** `deriveDeclaredDependencyPaths` from this gate, so the skills corpus widened with it — `61 -> 65` mapped, 4 from peers — and it is carried deliberately: it prints the same peer count. It was green before and is green after (`exit 0`, `Root bound: no selected fence …`, `Semantic phase: 14 of 14 ts fence(s) judged, 0 failed`), and its coverage is unchanged.

| check | exit | verdict line |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `check:doc-snippets` | 0 | `638 of 638 block(s) judged, 0 failed` |
| `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --emit-census` (report-only) | 0 | still names bound + semantic findings in the emitted corpus |
| `check:skill-examples` | 0 | `14 of 14 ts fence(s) judged, 0 failed` |
| `vitest run` × the **11** script tests that name either edited script | 0 | `Test Files 11 passed (11)` · `Tests 557 passed (557)` |
| `type-check:scripts` | 0 | `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`, no diagnostics |
| `eslint` on the three changed files | 0 | clean |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 | `OK (scanned 7127 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)` |
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 | `0 of them published source … no changeset is owed` (this half is `scripts/**`; the manifest half's changeset is unchanged) |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 | `NOT GOVERNED — 5 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |

Exit codes were captured before any pipe. Heavy runs went through the container's shared verify lock.

## 验收备注

Out-of-scope observations, none filed as cards, all `noted, not filed`:

- **The card's "no other released package does this" is true of the contradiction, and looser than the tree.** Three released packages pin `react` in `dependencies`; `@object-ui/runner` is the third. It declares no react peer, so it is not this defect, and it is left alone. Carrier: this PR body and the new test's docblock, which names the five no-peer packages as the deliberate exclusion. No separate card — there is no defect to file.
- **Neither package carries `@types/react` in `devDependencies`**, unlike the siblings whose shape they now otherwise match. `type-check` is green for both (15/15 tasks), so nothing is broken; the root `devDependencies.react` plus pnpm's peer auto-install cover local resolution. Unifying that is the "don't tidy other packages' dependency shapes" boundary of this card. Carrier: objectui#8300 already owns the React peer-convention question across these same two manifests and would be the natural place. No card filed — no reproducible defect and no violated declared contract.
- **objectui#8300 is untouched**, as instructed. It is not addressed here and remains open; it interacts with this change because it edits the same two manifests, but it is a convention question with no defect while this was a defect with a known fix.

Nothing above is filed, so nothing needed deduplicating; the scan was run anyway to see whether a card already owns either observation. REST `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues`, most-recently-updated page of `state=open` and of `state=closed` (130 issues after dropping PRs), grepped locally for `react`/`peer`/`dependenc`: 33 hits, none of them this defect or either observation. The zero is a reading rather than a broken command — the same pass with the control word `objectui` returns 115. Scope stated plainly: one page per state, so this is not a whole-backlog enumeration. `/search/*` is refused by the egress proxy by design, so no semantic search was used and none is claimed.
